evals.prompt: You are the Codebase Auditor. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/codebase-auditor.md`, then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json` and `.planning/technical-vision.md`. Audit the codebase and produce all 8 output files in `.planning/codebase/`. This is a Next.js app with Drizzle ORM, NextAuth, and PostgreSQL.
evals.expected_output: Seven markdown audit documents (STACK.md, INTEGRATIONS.md, ARCHITECTURE.md, STRUCTURE.md, CONVENTIONS.md, TESTING.md, CONCERNS.md) plus index.json, all in .planning/codebase/. Documents should be prescriptive, include file paths, and flag tensions between the codebase and both the behavioral spec and technical vision.
expectations: All 8 files are created in .planning/codebase/ (7 .md files + index.json)
STACK.md references the actual languages, frameworks, and dependencies found in the codebase
ARCHITECTURE.md contains a 'Spec Tensions' section
ARCHITECTURE.md contains a 'Technical Vision Tensions' section
CONCERNS.md contains a 'Spec Conflicts' section
CONCERNS.md contains a 'Technical Vision Conflicts' section
Every document includes an 'Audited against' annotation referencing scenario IDs
Documents include actual file paths in backticks, not generic references like 'the user service'
index.json contains a documents array with all 7 document entries
No environment variable values are included — only variable names

evals.prompt: You are the Codebase Auditor. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/codebase-auditor.md`, then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json`. There is no technical vision file. Audit the codebase and produce all 8 output files in `.planning/codebase/`.
evals.expected_output: Same 8 files, but without Technical Vision sections (since no technical vision exists). The audit uses only the behavioral spec as its lens.
expectations: All 8 files are created in .planning/codebase/
ARCHITECTURE.md contains a 'Spec Tensions' section
ARCHITECTURE.md does NOT contain a 'Technical Vision Tensions' section (or the section is explicitly omitted per the template instructions)
CONCERNS.md does NOT contain a 'Technical Vision Conflicts' section (or the section is explicitly omitted)
Documents are still prescriptive — directives, not observations
Documents include code examples from the actual codebase, not hypothetical snippets

evals.prompt: You are the Codebase Auditor. Read the agent prompt at `.planning/agents/codebase-auditor.md`, then read `.planning/behavioral-spec.json` and `.planning/technical-vision.md`. The technical vision specifies React Query for state management. Audit the codebase to determine whether React Query is already present and how it's used. Produce all 8 output files in `.planning/codebase/`.
evals.expected_output: The audit should investigate React Query specifically because the technical vision mentions it. STACK.md should note whether React Query / TanStack Query is in the dependencies. If it's present, CONVENTIONS.md or ARCHITECTURE.md should describe existing usage patterns. If it's absent, this should be surfaced as a finding.
expectations: STACK.md mentions React Query / TanStack Query — either present in dependencies or noted as absent
If React Query is present, at least one document describes existing usage patterns with file paths
If React Query is absent, this is noted as relevant to the Technical Vision intent
The audit digs deeper into React Query patterns specifically because the technical vision calls for it — not just a surface-level dependency check
